story.objective.photo.title: The Missing Face
story.objective.photo.text: Examine the faded photograph on the central reading desk.
story.objective.corridor.title: The Ruined Corridor
story.objective.corridor.text: Study the mural and the records, then align the seals on the three plinths.
story.objective.vault.title: The Sealed Vault
story.objective.vault.text: Find the erased name in the vault’s signature register.
story.objective.return.title: The Way Back
story.objective.return.text: Unfasten the latch south of the manuscript archive to open the way back to the main hall.
story.objective.restoration.title: The Empty Place in the Photograph
story.objective.restoration.text: Take the shortcut back to the central reading desk and restore the name.
story.objective.complete.title: A Name Restored
story.objective.complete.text: Scribe Ian’s name and his last promise have returned.
story.action.mural: Read the marks on the mural
story.event.photo-found:
Someone has been erased from the photograph. There are words on the back.
“My name is in the register in the sealed vault.”
Beyond the northern arch, the corridor to the eastern manuscript archive opens. Lanterns flare on the twin gate towers.
story.event.mural-read:
A hand bearing a flame on the left. A scribe’s quill in the middle. A wave on the right.
“Find it by firelight, write it with a quill, send it away on a wave.”
story.event.seal-closed:
The seal trembles, then falls still.
Look again at the positions on the mural and the marks on the plinths.
story.event.seal-opened:
The three marks join and the vault door opens.
In the western workshop, freshly folded sheets hang on the drying rack.
story.event.ledger-read:
The name in the signature register is Ian.
Book spines return, one by one, to the empty manuscript shelves.
“I will stay by your side until the last reading.”
The ink wakes behind you. Find the latch to the south.
story.event.shortcut-opened:
The latch slides free. The pulley at the freight landing starts hoisting book crates again.
Follow the passage south of the manuscript archive through the western door to the familiar reading room.
story.event.name-restored: Ian. As you write the name beneath the photograph, the missing figure returns. “I’m late, but let me tell you the last story.”
story.prologue.stars:
The cold stars kept watch over me.
I used to look back at them in peace.
story.prologue.suns:
I did not fear the cold light falling from the stars,
nor the heat of suns that burned like fire,
story.prologue.dark:
nor even the dark that swallowed every light.
I feared none of it.
story.prologue.cold:
What is this terrible chill,
this cold that could freeze the world?
story.prologue.fear:
Why am I only now afraid?
The universe has not changed.
story.prologue.forgotten: What is it that I am forgetting?
story.prologue.photo.alt: In the faded photograph, the figure on the right has been erased, leaving a white silhouette.
story.folio-first-catalog.title: The First Catalog
story.folio-first-catalog.hint: Look on the small stand between the south door and the bookshelves.
story.folio-first-catalog.description: The archive’s first catalog lists people’s names before it lists book titles. Beneath each name, it records who first remembered that person and where they sat to read the memory.
story.folio-first-catalog.inscription: If you have forgotten a name, find the place where they sat.
story.folio-watch-roll.title: The Night Roll Call
story.folio-watch-roll.hint: The watch roll lies on the first reading desk in the west wing.
story.folio-watch-roll.description: Each night a guard walked the walls and counted the lanterns. The total never changes in the register, but on the last three pages it takes a few more steps to walk from one lantern to the next.
story.folio-watch-roll.inscription: If you see one lantern too many, turn back without counting it.
story.folio-stargazer.title: The Stargazer’s Journal
story.folio-stargazer.hint: Follow the curved rampart up from the plaza. Look on the western parapet of the round observatory.
story.folio-stargazer.description: The stargazer measured each night against the band of the galaxy beyond the walls. Then the little stars in the west began to vanish and return in the same order, though the band itself never changed. On the last page, the observer crossed the entry out of the weather column and left a line for it elsewhere.
story.folio-stargazer.inscription: What moved first in the place that stayed dark the longest?
story.folio-bindery.title: The Bookbinder’s Repair Slip
story.folio-bindery.hint: Enter the workshop west of the plaza and examine the workbench by the door.
story.folio-bindery.description: Unpick the broken threads. Mend the tears with thin paper. At the foot of the slip is a promise to return the book before the last reading. The space for its title is blank, but the pen left its impression in the paper.
story.folio-bindery.inscription: First ask who is waiting for the book.
story.folio-freight.title: Star Route Cargo Receipt
story.folio-freight.hint: Look on the book crate against the south wall at the back of the storehouse.
story.folio-freight.description: It took three people to lift a crate out of empty space. One wound the rope, one recorded the weight, and the last called out the titles of the books that had returned. The handwriting in the recipient’s box is always the same.
story.folio-freight.inscription: One crate, twenty-three volumes. The voices went uncounted.
story.folio-ink.title: On the Preservation of Black Ink
story.folio-ink.hint: Once inside the corridor, examine the stone wall opposite the mural.
story.folio-ink.description: Even held to a flame, the archive’s black ink never dries. When no one remembers the event on the page, the letters sink one by one into the black from which they came. This is why people gather in the reading hall to read the same sentence aloud.
story.folio-ink.inscription: What must endure is the person who remembers the ink.
story.folio-unreturned.title: The Unreturned Book
story.folio-unreturned.hint: Open the seal, then examine the wall between the original manuscripts on the west shelves.
story.folio-unreturned.description: One box in the return register has long stood empty. The journal says the borrower will come back one day. Each day someone dusted the shelf so that no one else would take the book’s place.
story.folio-unreturned.inscription: If you are still reading, leave the date blank.
story.folio-return-plan.title: A Map for the Homeward Journey
story.folio-return-plan.hint: Beyond the latch, examine the north wall of the passage leading to the main hall.
story.folio-return-plan.description: One line leads away from the archive. Three lead back. In the margins, the mapmaker recorded what they saw on the way home in place of the building’s dimensions. At the end of the shortest path stands a bookshelf anyone would recognize.
story.folio-return-plan.inscription: When you open the last door, choose the first book you remember.
story.title: Return to title
story.ending: Chapter One · The Person Erased from the Photograph
story.ward: The shadow cannot cross the silver ward.
